messages:
maria: Heads up — since ~08:12 UTC we're seeing 503s from model-serving in eu-west-2 when code tries to reach Secrets Manager via the interface VPC endpoint. Other regions fine. Pods hit the private IP but the TLS handshake never completes.

sam: Any recent route table/NAT changes?

maria: Not from infra-team. No route changes. But I noticed all SecretsManager endpoint ENIs in eu-west-2 have a different SG now (sg-0bcd0001). Previously they were sg-eb1200ff which allowed pod-subnet -> 443.

alex: Can you paste the ENI list and SG describe?

maria: Sure:

```
$ aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters Name=description,Values="*com.amazonaws.eu-west-2.secretsmanager*" --query 'NetworkInterfaces[*].{Id:NetworkInterfaceId,SG:Groups[0].GroupId,Subnet:SubnetId}' -o table
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
| DescribeNetworkInterfaces                                               |
|-------------------+----------------+-------------------------------|
| eni-0abc1234      | sg-0bcd0001    | subnet-0aa111                 |
| eni-0def5678      | sg-0bcd0001    | subnet-0bb222                 |
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

$ aws ec2 describe-security-groups --group-ids sg-0bcd0001 --query 'SecurityGroups[*].{Id:GroupId,Ingress:IpPermissions, Egress:IpPermissionsEgress}' -o json
[{"Id":"sg-0bcd0001","Ingress":[],"Egress":[]}]
```

maria: So the SG has no ingress/egress rules (Terraform drift?). Pods resolve endpoint to ENI private IP but connections fail because the endpoint ENI SG is locked down.

lee: For interface endpoints you need the endpoint ENI SG to allow inbound from the pod CIDR to 443 (and ephemeral ports might be needed). If SG was replaced with a default deny, that explains timeouts.

josh: Also interesting: existing TCP connections from pods to that endpoint were stuck in conntrack with the old ENI IPs, so new ENI SG change caused packets to be dropped but conntrack still mapping to old tuples — we saw half-open entries on nodes.

maria: I checked one node: `sudo conntrack -L | grep 172.31.12.45` (endpoint IP) and there were a bunch of ESTABLISHED entries lingering from before the change.

alex: Steps to fix?

josh: Two quick mitigations:
- reapply correct SG to the VPC endpoint ENIs (or attach the previous SG)
- flush conntrack / restart kube-proxy on affected nodes so stale entries are removed

maria: I rolled the SG back to sg-eb1200ff (the one referenced in the tf state backup) and then ran on the 3 affected nodes:
```
sudo conntrack -D -d 172.31.12.45  # flush entries for the endpoint ip
sudo systemctl restart kube-proxy
```

maria: After that pods' requests to Secrets Manager started succeeding within ~30s. Errors dropped to 0.

sam: Nice. Who accidentally applied the SG change? We should track root cause (tf apply from security?).

maria: Appears to be a mis-scoped security team tf change that included a `aws_security_group_rule` with a wildcard update. Reverting was manual; opened a quick PR to scope it properly.

infra-bot: Created incident INC-3982 for Privatelink failure in eu-west-2 — https://incidents.redwood/INC-3982 :rotating_light:

alex: Follow-ups:
- add a pre-apply plan check to disallow replacing endpoint SGs without +owner approval
- add healthcheck alert that queries interface endpoint ENI SGs vs expected SG id (per region)
- consider a conntrack drain playbook for node-level fixes (documented in runbook)

lee: Also add a k8s readiness check to call secretsmanager for a short TTL so deployments degrade gracefully if secrets can't be retrieved.

maria: Agreed. I'll file the Terraform guard PR and update the runbook with the conntrack commands and sequence.

sam: 👍 thanks for the quick triage and rollback.

josh: :thumbsup: nice catch on the SG swap, conntrack would have fooled people into thinking it was something else.

maria: Marking resolved for now, will keep the incident open until we have the PR/monitoring in place.
